text:
Devon: quick ping — PR #9123 introduces a scheduling tweak. canaries show a throughput drop and mem uplift.
Devon: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pr/9123
Devon: bench summary (small sample):
```
model: /redwood/open-4b
config: microbatch=8, seq=2048
baseline p95: 112ms -> candidate p95: 121ms (+8%)
baseline throughput: 235 req/s -> candidate: 205 req/s (-12%)
baseline max_rss: 28.1GB -> candidate: 31.4GB (+11.7%)
``` 
Mia: yikes, 8% p95 and 12% throughput hit is not great. did you run with adaptive-batcher off? 
Devon: yes - adaptive-batcher=off. also tried with no-tiling and saw similar delta. attaching raw artifacts: http://ci.internal/bench/9123/artifacts
Sam: can you paste the exact kernel/quant settings used? tiny changes there can shift perf
Devon: kernel=triton_v3, quant=fp16, matmul=auto
Asha: @Sam I can eyeball the flamegraph if you want — add it to the artifact
Sam: please also include the canary comparison plot (p95 over time). helps rule out noise
Devon: CI Bot ran canary: http://ci.internal/canary/9123 — CI Bot: canary finished (10/10 nodes), regression flagged
CI Bot: canary results: p95 increase 7.9%, throughput -11.8%, rss +11.7% — detailed CSV attached
Mia: sounds like we should hold merge. @Devon can you create a rollback plan if we can't land in next window?
Devon: will do. plan: revert scheduling change, run quick canary, and open follow-up to try smaller change
Asha: happy to review rollback PR and run the flamegraphs
Sam: +1 from me once rollback PR has perf run attached
Devon: thanks all — ping here when you have a minute to look at the rollback (PR #9130)
Mia: will check in ~30m
